(3) REQ-102's real orchestration is explicitly bound to call `deriveRecentSpawnAttempts({ledgerRows: readChildren(...)})` directly, never a hand-rolled reimplementation (behavioral-spec.md:685-690, 767-771; verification-architecture.md Purity Boundary Map row for `decideColonySpawn`, line 148; PROP-102g, line 312; Gate item (1f), lines 646-656) -- mirroring REQ-101's own `filterProductiveCitizens` integration discipline exactly. (4) The three new proof obligations are each specific and binding enough to genuinely catch an implementation bug: PROP-102f's four-case fixture (verification-architecture.md:311) pins exact expected `ts`/`outcome` values per case including the success-then-bootstrap_failed case's requirement that `ts` remain the ORIGINAL `attempted_ms` and that no second entry ever appears; PROP-102g (verification-architecture.md:312) requires both a Tier-1 control-flow read AND a Tier-2 integration test appending real rows to a real `ledger.js` file and asserting the real output matches PROP-102f's fixture-level expectations exactly; PROP-305h (verification-architecture.md:380) requires a structural grep confirming no code path calls `Date.now()`/generates a new timestamp for a non-first row, plus a 3-row real-data fixture. FIND-1401 is genuinely and completely resolved with no residual gap.
